justice: Most visible street space is allocated to multiple wide motor-vehicle lanes, while the pedestrian realm on the right appears narrow and set back, indicating an uneven distribution of space across road users.

sustainability: Continuous planted medians, roadside trees, and vegetated strips provide urban greenery that can support shade, air-quality benefits, and ecological value.

aesthetics: The avenue has a strong visual order created by symmetrical streetlights, consistent lane geometry, and continuous planted medians.
Rows of mature and young trees on the right side soften the road edge and improve the overall landscape quality.
The pavement, curbs, planting beds, and roadway markings appear clean and well maintained, contributing to a neat and coherent streetscape.
comfort: Roadside trees provide some shade along the right-side path, which can improve thermal comfort for users off the carriageway.
